obligations.title: Software Safety Classification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall assign a software safety class (Class A, B, or C) to
the SOFTWARE SYSTEM based on the severity of HAZARDOUS SITUATION that could
result if the SOFTWARE SYSTEM should fail to behave as specified."
extracted_requirements: Assign IEC 62304 safety class (A, B, or C) to each software item before development begins
Document the classification rationale referencing ISO 14971 severity levels
Record the classification in the Software Development Plan or a dedicated classification record
Re-evaluate classification if intended use or hazard analysis changes

obligations.title: Software Development Plan
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall establish a SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT PLAN for conducting
the activities of the software development process."
extracted_requirements: Establish a Software Development Plan (SDP) before beginning software development
SDP may be part of the Design and Development Plan or a separate document
SDP must be updated to reflect actual development activities throughout the project

obligations.title: SDP Content & Lifecycle
obligations.verbatim:
"The SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT PLAN shall address: (a) the software development life cycle
model including the activities and tasks to be performed and their sequencing;
(b) the deliverables of the software development process and the criteria for their
acceptance; (c) the standards, methods, and tools to be used; (d) traceability
between software requirements and software system test cases."
extracted_requirements: SDP must define the SDLC model (waterfall, iterative, agile-within-waterfall, etc.)
SDP must list planned deliverables with acceptance criteria for each
SDP must identify development standards, methods, and tools (including tool validation status)
SDP must describe the traceability approach from requirements to test cases
SDP must address configuration management, problem resolution, and risk management integration

obligations.title: Software Requirements Specification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall define and document the SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS from the
SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS and the results of RISK MANAGEMENT activities."
extracted_requirements: Define software requirements traceable to system-level requirements
Define software requirements traceable to risk management outputs (risk controls implemented in software)
Document requirements in a Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

obligations.title: SRS Content Requirements
extracted_requirements: SRS must cover: functional/capability requirements, I/O requirements, external interfaces
SRS must address software-controlled alarms, warnings, and messages
SRS must include cybersecurity and usability requirements (for Class II SaMD)
All requirements must be verifiable (have defined acceptance criteria or test method)

obligations.title: SRS Risk Control Trace
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall re-evaluate the RISK associated with the software
after establishing the SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS and update the RISK MANAGEMENT
FILE as necessary."
extracted_requirements: Re-evaluate risk after SRS is established — update risk file if new hazards emerge
Document this re-evaluation step in the risk management file or SRS changelog

obligations.title: Software Architecture Specification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall transform the SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS into a documented
architecture that describes the structure of the software and identifies the
SOFTWARE ITEMS."
extracted_requirements: Produce a Software Architecture Document (SAD) transforming the SRS into a structural design
SAD must identify and name all software items (decomposition to the unit level is not required at this stage)
SAD must describe the interfaces between software items and between the software and hardware/external systems

obligations.title: SOUP Identification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall identify SOUP items including: (a) the title, manufacturer,
and unique SOUP designator; (b) the requirements for the SOUP item."
extracted_requirements: Identify all SOUP (Software of Unknown Provenance) items used in each software item
For each SOUP item: document title, manufacturer/supplier, version, and required functional/performance requirements
Maintain a SOUP list as a controlled document — update on each SOUP change

obligations.title: Architecture Verification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall verify that the software architecture implements all
software requirements and identify potential causes of hazardous situations."
extracted_requirements: Conduct and document an architecture verification that confirms all SRS requirements are addressed in the design
As part of architecture verification, evaluate whether the architecture could cause or fail to mitigate hazardous situations
Record the verification outcome (pass/fail per requirement) in the SAD or a separate verification record

obligations.title: Detailed Software Design
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall refine the software architecture until it is represented
by SOFTWARE UNITS that can be implemented and verified."
extracted_requirements: Decompose the architecture into software units (leaf-level components that can be individually implemented and tested)
Document the detailed design for each software unit with sufficient detail to permit implementation without ambiguity
Verify that the detailed design implements the software architecture (no requirement left unaddressed)

obligations.title: Unit Verification
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall verify SOFTWARE UNITS. The verification shall confirm that
the units implement the design and are free of common programming errors."
extracted_requirements: Verify each software unit through code review, unit testing, or both
Class C: unit testing is required; define test cases per the detailed design
Class B: code review of each unit is sufficient (testing not mandated but recommended)
Record verification results — pass/fail per unit, reviewer/tester identity, date

obligations.title: Integration Testing
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall integrate the SOFTWARE ITEMS and verify that the
integrated SOFTWARE ITEMS implement the software architecture and satisfy
the SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS."
extracted_requirements: Produce an integration plan defining the sequence and method for integrating software items
Conduct integration testing at each integration step and upon full integration
Integration tests must verify that integrated software satisfies the SRS
Document integration test results with pass/fail per test case and anomalies found

obligations.title: System Testing
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall test the SOFTWARE SYSTEM for conformance to the SOFTWARE
REQUIREMENTS. The testing shall include boundary conditions and stress conditions
and shall check for ANOMALIES."
extracted_requirements: Test the complete integrated software system against every SRS requirement
Test must include normal operating conditions, boundary conditions, stress conditions, and foreseeable misuse
Document a System Test Plan before testing begins; document results in a System Test Report
All test anomalies must be evaluated and resolved before release

obligations.title: Software Release
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall ensure that the software is released only when: all
software development activities are complete; the software configuration
is documented; known ANOMALIES are evaluated and their impact on safety
is acceptable; the software version identifier is assigned."
extracted_requirements: Assign a unique version identifier to the released software (must be traceable in the DHF)
Document all known anomalies at release with their safety impact evaluation
Produce a release checklist confirming all §5 development activities are complete
Record the released configuration (version of each software item, SOUP versions, build environment)

obligations.title: Software Maintenance Plan
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall establish and document a SOFTWARE MAINTENANCE PLAN.
The plan shall address: problem and modification analysis; modification
implementation; release of modifications."
extracted_requirements: Establish a Software Maintenance Plan (may be part of SDP or a separate document)
Maintenance plan must address: how post-market problems are analyzed, how modifications are scoped and implemented, how modified releases are managed
PCCP changes must follow the maintenance process — classify the change, evaluate safety impact, implement per §5 process appropriate to the classification

obligations.title: Software Hazard Analysis
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall identify SOFTWARE ITEMS that could contribute to a
HAZARDOUS SITUATION. For each such SOFTWARE ITEM, the MANUFACTURER shall
evaluate the contribution of the SOFTWARE ITEM to the HAZARDOUS SITUATION."
extracted_requirements: For each hazardous situation in the risk file, identify which software items could contribute to it
Evaluate how and to what degree each software item contributes (causal analysis)
Document results in a software risk analysis record — typically a software FMEA or hazard analysis table

obligations.title: SOUP Risk Evaluation
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall evaluate the ANOMALY LISTS and reported PROBLEMS for
SOUP items and shall determine whether the anomalies or reported problems are
relevant to the SOFTWARE SYSTEM and document the conclusions."
extracted_requirements: For each SOUP item, obtain and review the supplier's known anomaly list
Evaluate whether any known anomaly could affect the safety of the software system
Document the evaluation conclusion (relevant / not relevant / mitigated) in the risk management file
Repeat evaluation when a new SOUP version is adopted or new anomalies are reported

obligations.title: Software Configuration Management
extracted_requirements: Establish a Configuration Management Plan (may be part of SDP)
CM plan must define: what is a configuration item, how items are labeled/versioned, how changes are controlled, how configuration status is tracked
Configuration items must include: software items, test cases, tools, SOUP versions, build scripts, and DHF documents

obligations.title: Problem Resolution Process
obligations.verbatim:
"The MANUFACTURER shall establish and document a SOFTWARE PROBLEM RESOLUTION
PROCESS that includes: problem reporting, analysis, resolution and verification,
release of modified software, communication of resolution to relevant parties."
extracted_requirements: Establish a problem resolution process covering: receipt, investigation, resolution, and closure
Each problem must be evaluated for: safety impact, causal analysis, resolution approach
Problem resolution records must be maintained — linked to the affected software version and release
Post-market problems feed back into the risk management file when they reveal new hazards

obligations.title: Software Traceability
obligations.verbatim:
"The SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT PLAN shall address traceability between: software
requirements and system requirements; software requirements and software system
tests; software requirements and software architecture; and for Class C, between
software requirements and software units."
extracted_requirements: Maintain bidirectional traceability: system requirements → software requirements → architecture → test cases
Class C additional: software requirements → individual software units
Document the traceability approach in the SDP
Produce a trace matrix as the formal traceability deliverable
